name: Insteon USB Wireless Adapter
description: The serial commands of the Insteon USB Wireless Adapters 2448A7 and 2448A7H, an RF-only modem with no SET button: the modem commands that apply, without Send X10.

serialCommands.name: getImInfo
serialCommands.description: Asks the modem for its Insteon ID, device category, device subcategory and firmware version. The modem returns the values hard-coded at the factory, whatever Set Host Device Category set.

reply.name: id
reply.description: The modem's Insteon ID, high byte first.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.name: startAllLinkingAsResponder
serialCommands.description: Puts the modem into ALL-Linking mode without the SET button, to link as a responder. The modem's LED blinks until the ALL-Link completes or is canceled, and an ALL-Linking Completed message reports the link.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes name Start ALL-Linking (0x64) as the way to start linking mode, but not its control bytes; this control byte is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives.

serialCommands.name: startAllLinkingAsController
serialCommands.description: Puts the modem into ALL-Linking mode without the SET button, to link as a controller. The modem's LED blinks until the ALL-Link completes or is canceled, and an ALL-Linking Completed message reports the link.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes name Start ALL-Linking (0x64) as the way to start linking mode, but not its control bytes; this control byte is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives.

serialCommands.name: startAllLinkingAsEither
serialCommands.description: Puts the modem into ALL-Linking mode without the SET button, to link as a controller when the modem starts ALL-Linking and as a responder when another device does. The modem's LED blinks until the ALL-Link completes or is canceled, and an ALL-Linking Completed message reports the link.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes name Start ALL-Linking (0x64) as the way to start linking mode, but not its control bytes; this control byte is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives.

serialCommands.name: deleteAllLink
serialCommands.description: Deletes the ALL-Link to a device for a group, through ALL-Linking mode.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes name Start ALL-Linking (0x64) as the way to enter linking mode, but not its control bytes; this control byte is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives.

serialCommands.name: cancelAllLinking
serialCommands.description: Cancels ALL-Linking mode started with Start ALL-Linking. The adapter has no SET button to start it.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.name: setHostDeviceCategory
serialCommands.description: Sets the device category and subcategory of the host, which the modem sends other devices while ALL-Linking. The modem keeps them across a power loss; Get IM Info still returns the factory values.

parameters.name: firmware
parameters.description: The host's firmware version, or a filler byte.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.name: resetModem
serialCommands.description: Puts the modem in its factory reset state, which clears its entire ALL-Link database. The ACK follows the erase, about 20 seconds for a modem with external EEPROM and about 2 seconds for one without.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.name: setAckMessageByte
serialCommands.description: Sets the byte the modem puts in cmd2 of the ACK it sends automatically after an Insteon direct message. The host has about 15 milliseconds after the message to send it.

parameters.name: command2
parameters.description: The byte for cmd2 of the ACK.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.name: getFirstAllLinkRecord
serialCommands.description: Starts a scan of the modem's ALL-Link database. An ACK means an ALL-Link Record Response follows; a NAK means the database is empty.

verification.note: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U but list no commands, so this entry is carried from the modem command set, which the Insteon Modem Developer's Guide gives, and no document confirms the adapter answers it.

serialCommands.description: Returns the next record in the modem's ALL-Link database. An ACK means an ALL-Link Record Response follows; a NAK means there are no more records.

serialCommands.name: setImConfiguration
serialCommands.description: Sets all of the modem's configuration flags at once. Reading them with Get IM Configuration first lets a caller change one bit.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: The configuration flags; bits 3 to 0 are reserved and stay 0.

bits.name: autoLinkingDisabled
bits.description: Disables automatic ALL-Linking when the SET button is pressed and held.

bits.name: monitorMode
bits.description: Reports every received message whose From Address is in the modem's ALL-Link database, not only those directed to the modem.

bits.name: ledControlledByHost
bits.description: Disables the modem's automatic LED operation, so the host controls the LED with LED On and LED Off.

bits.name: deadmanDisabled
bits.description: Allows the host to wait more than 240 milliseconds between bytes it sends the modem.

serialCommands.description: Searches the modem's ALL-Link database from the top for the first record that matches the group and ID, ignoring the record flags, and returns it in an ALL-Link Record Response. A NAK means no record matches.

bits.name: inUse

bits.name: controller

bits.name: usedBefore

parameters.name: group

notes: The USB Wireless Adapter Developer Notes (2010-07-02) say the adapter has the same communication protocol as the PowerLinc USB 2414U, with these changes: device category 0x03 and subcategory 0x1F; no SET button, so linking mode starts from software with Start ALL-Linking (0x64); RF only, so it needs a dual-band device to reach powerline devices; and no X10, so Send X10 (0x63) is NAKed in every case and X10 Received (0x52) is never sent. The document lists no other commands.

The entries are the modem command set's, minus sendX10. Nothing in the document confirms them, so each carries inferred, except that the document does name Start ALL-Linking (0x64); its control bytes are still carried.
sendX10 is left out: the adapter NAKs every frame with command number 0x63, and the schema has no marker for a command that always fails.
The document describes the 2448A7 and no document names the 2448A7H, so the 2448A7H's use of this set is inferred.
Entries that mention the SET button, such as the autoLinkingDisabled bit of setImConfiguration, are the modem's; the adapter has no SET button, so that bit has nothing to disable.

A serial command is 0x02, its number and its payload; the modem echoes it and ends the echo with an ACK (0x06) or a NAK (0x15). Send Insteon Standard or Extended Message (0x62) and Send ALL-Link Command (0x61) carry a device message, so the device's own command set describes them and they are not entries.
Start ALL-Linking and Manage ALL-Link Record are one entry per control byte, so each control byte has its own effect; effects follow the modem command set's.
